newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wins Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania - TV.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wins Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania - TV.

text.p: President Bill Clinton won the crucial states of Illinois, Michigan and Pennsylvania in the U.S. election, according to projections by several television networks on Tuesday.

Illinois, with 22 electoral college votes, is a bellwether in U.S. presidential elections, going with the winner in every election except two in the past century. Michigan has 18 electoral college votes while Pennsylvania has 23. A total of 270 is needed to win the election.
Separately, the television networks projected Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole had won the following four states: Texas, Oklahoma, Alabama and his home state of Kansas.
Texas had a whopping 32 electoral college votes, Oklahoma eight, Alabama nine and Kansas six.
Dole had been expected to win all four.

Separately, the CNN and NBC television networks reported that Dole had also won Indiana, a bedrock conservative state which earlier in the evening had appeared to close to call. Indiana has 12 electoral votes.
